meta.title: Satarka — Nepal Disaster Alerts & Preparedness

home.title: Know the risk before the water rises.
home.body: Satarka gathers Nepal's official hazard feeds into one place, in Nepali and English, and turns them into plain language you can act on. It supplements official warnings — it does not replace them.
home.disclaimer: In an emergency, follow the instructions of local authorities and official warnings.

home.learnTeaserBody: What causes each hazard, the local warning signs, and what to do before, during, and after.

about.title: About Satarka
about.missionBody: In Nepal, hazards and the alerts about them are scattered across many agencies, languages, and websites. Satarka brings the official feeds together in one place — in Nepali and English — and explains each one plainly, so a person can act before the water rises, not after.
about.honestyBody: A false sense of security is more dangerous than an honest gap. We only label something “live” when a real feed backs it. Everything else is marked reference, report, or no-feed, with a link to the official source.
about.methodologyBody: On the server, every feed is fetched, cleaned, and mapped into one shared alert schema. Each alert keeps the name and link of the agency that produced it, its status (live, recent, reference, report, no-feed), and the moment we last checked. The browser never talks to third-party hosts directly — it only talks to Satarka's own API, so a failing feed degrades the page honestly instead of breaking it.
about.licensesBody: Satarka is built on public data: DHM hydrology, NDRRMA BIPAD, USGS earthquake events, GDACS alerts, ICIMOD glacial-lake inventories, and ReliefWeb reports. Base maps are © OpenStreetMap contributors. Source licenses apply to the underlying data; our normalisation and text are original to this project.
about.rasuwaBody1: On 26 August 2026 a catastrophic flash flood struck the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors in Rasuwa. Investigators from ICIMOD and DHM determined it was not a classic glacial lake outburst: a massive rock-and-ice avalanche from the north face of Langtang Lirung dammed the Lhende Khola, and when that temporary dam burst it released a violent surge downstream.
about.rasuwaBody2: The flood destroyed homes, markets, hydropower plants (Chilime, Trishuli) and the Prithvi Highway, killing more than 900 people. Early accounts called it a GLOF; the science later corrected the story. That correction is exactly why Satarka exists — the honest label matters, because people act on the word they hear.
about.rasuwaBody3: The lesson: river risk in steep valleys is not only about gauges or glacial lakes. Slopes upstream can collapse and flood a valley within minutes. Our guides and the map are built around that reality — move to high ground early, and never wait for a warning to leave.
about.disclaimerBody: Satarka aggregates and explains publicly available hazard information. It supplements official warnings and does not replace them. In an emergency, follow the instructions of local authorities.

disclaimerModal.title: Important Public Safety Disclaimer
disclaimerModal.lead: Satarka is an independent civic information platform that aggregates open data from government departments and scientific agencies. It does not replace official emergency channels.
disclaimerModal.primaryDirectiveBody: Satarka is not an official warning service. In the event of a flood, landslide, earthquake, or extreme weather, always follow instructions, sirens, evacuations, and SMS alerts from the Nepal Police, Armed Police Force, local municipal disaster committees (LDMC), and the Ministry of Home Affairs (NDRRMA).
disclaimerModal.aggregationBody: Information is aggregated from the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM), NDRRMA BIPAD, USGS, GDACS, ICIMOD, and ReliefWeb. Feeds refresh automatically, but upstream latency or communication delays may occur.
disclaimerModal.sensorGapsTitle: 3. Absence of an Alert Does Not Mean Zero Risk
disclaimerModal.sensorGapsBody: Torrential rain, cloudbursts, and upstream landslides can dam tributaries or knock out telemetry sensors and mobile towers within minutes. If you observe rising water, sudden river silence, slope cracking, or unusual rumbling, evacuate immediately to high ground.
